intro.en: Systematic reading of chest, neck, abdominal and bone films plus the classic signs asked in the paediatric practical exam.

items.summary: Stepwise check of a child chest film: depth of breath, view, exposure, rotation, soft tissues and lung zones before naming any disease.

blocks.title: Breath, view and exposure
bullets: Accept a mid breath film: the right dome should sit near the 6th rib in front and the 9th-10th rib behind.
Newborns are filmed front to back (AP view).
Once the child can sit or stand alone, prefer back to front (PA view).
Films lying on the side (decubitus) help prove pleural fluid.
Exposure is right when the spine and disc gaps show down to T3 or T4; seeing further means overexposure.

blocks.title: Rotation, cage and zones
bullets: Judge rotation by clavicle shape and place, and by matching the front ends of lower ribs on both sides.
Scan soft tissues and the bony cage; wiped out costophrenic angles mean fluid or pleural thickening.
Split each lung into upper, middle and lower zones with lines drawn from the 2nd and 4th ribs.
Describe each zone in terms of white patches, overfilling, collapse and similar words.

viva.q: How do you confirm a satisfactory breath on film?
viva.a: Right dome near the 6th rib in front and the 9th-10th rib behind.

viva.q: When is an AP view used instead of PA?
viva.a: In newborns; PA follows once the child sits or stands alone.
Seeing spine and disc gaps below T3 or T4.
By horizontal lines drawn from the 2nd and 4th ribs.

image.brief: Normal child chest X-ray front view with rib numbers, zone lines from the 2nd and 4th ribs, and the diaphragmatic dome level marked, on a dark film background.

title.en: Chest film signs and heart patterns

items.summary: What each shadow means: air leaks, silhouette loss, hernia through the diaphragm and the heart shapes of left to right versus right to left shunts.

blocks.title: Air, silhouette and shifted organs
bullets: Pneumothorax is air in the pleural space: a dark rim with lung collapse and zero lung markings inside, unlike emphysema.
Lost left heart border (silhouette sign) means lingular collapse or consolidation.
Lost right heart border means right middle lobe collapse or consolidation.
Study the hilar, mediastinal and cardiac shadows for nodes and for shift of the midline.

blocks.title: Hernia and heart disease clues
bullets: Diaphragmatic hernia from birth: air filled bowel loops in one chest half with part of the diaphragm missing and shift to the other side.
A cardiothoracic ratio above 0.55 suggests an enlarged heart.
Left to right shunt disease: big heart with left ventricular bulk (LVH) and crowded lung vessels (plethoric fields).
Tetralogy of Fallot with right to left shunt: big heart with right ventricular bulk (RVH, boot shaped heart) and pale lung fields (oligaemic).

viva.q: How does pneumothorax differ from emphysema on film?
viva.a: Pneumothorax is a dark rim with total loss of lung markings inside.

viva.q: What does each silhouette sign localise?
viva.a: Left border loss means lingular disease; right border loss means middle lobe disease.

viva.q: How do shunt patterns differ on film?
viva.a: Left to right gives LVH with plethoric fields; Fallot gives boot shaped RVH with oligaemic fields.

image.brief: Child chest X-ray showing a dark air rim of pneumothorax along one edge with absent markings, arrows marking the collapsed lung edge, dark film background.

items.summary: Five patterns of food pipe and windpipe misjoining, led by the common type with a blind upper pouch and a lower joining, hinted by extra liquor and a single cord artery.

blocks.title: Types
bullets: Five types of TEF (tracheo-oesophageal fistula) are recognised.
The commonest type, about 80 percent: the upper food pipe ends blind and the lower part joins the windpipe.
Extra liquor in pregnancy (maternal polyhydramnios) gives a clue.
A single umbilical artery gives a further clue.

viva.a: Blind ending upper oesophagus with the lower part joined to the trachea; about 80 percent.

viva.q: Which antenatal clues point to it?
viva.a: Maternal polyhydramnios and a single umbilical artery.

image.brief: Side view diagram of a newborn chest and neck showing a blind upper food pipe pouch and a lower channel joining the windpipe, plain background with parts labelled.

title.en: Lateral neck X-ray: croup and epiglottitis

items.summary: Two cannot miss neck signs on the side view film: the steeple of croup and the thumbprint of epiglottitis.

blocks.title: Two signs
bullets: Read the side (lateral) neck film.
Croup: steeple sign from narrowing below the voice box (subglottic narrowing).
Epiglottitis: thumbprint sign from a swollen epiglottis.

viva.a: An enlarged epiglottis seen in epiglottitis.

image.brief: Side view neck X-ray diagram of a small child with a pointed steeple narrowing below the voice box on one side and a swollen thumb shaped epiglottis on the other, labelled.

items.summary: Two gas patterns on the erect belly film: free air with levels means leaked gut, while levels alone mean blocked gut.

blocks.title: Two patterns
bullets: Gas under the diaphragm plus many air fluid levels suggests belly infection (peritonitis) from gut perforation or necrotising enterocolitis (NEC).
Many air fluid levels within the bowel without free air suggests intestinal obstruction.

viva.q: What does gas under the diaphragm with levels mean?

image.brief: Erect child abdominal X-ray showing a thin crescent of free gas under the diaphragm and step ladder air fluid levels in the bowel, arrows marked, dark film background.

items.summary: How to scan a child bone film end to shaft to soft tissue, and the widening, cupping and bending that spells rickets.

blocks.title: Reading the film
bullets: Study the epiphysis (end), diaphysis (shaft), metaphysis (growing junction) and soft tissue in turn.
Normally the combined width of both cortices equals the width of the medulla (marrow cavity).

blocks.title: Rickets signs
bullets: Wider gap between epiphysis and metaphysis.
Cupping, fraying (blurring) and splaying (widening) of the metaphysis edge.
Fractures of weakened bone.
Bending of long bones, beaded ribs (rickety rosary) and skull bossing.
Thinning of bone shadow (rarefaction).

viva.q: What four parts do you check on a bone film?
viva.a: Epiphysis, diaphysis, metaphysis and soft tissue.

viva.q: What is the normal cortex to medulla rule?
viva.a: Both cortices together equal the medulla in width.

viva.q: Name three rickets signs at the metaphysis.
viva.a: Cupping, fraying and splaying with a wider gap.

image.brief: Child wrist X-ray showing a widened growth plate with cupped and frayed metaphysis edges beside a normal wrist for contrast, dark film background, labelled.
